A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ULTra research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and the equations, tables, and figures can be matched despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original segmentation results, token perturbation experiments, object-selection measurements, and qualitative LLM analyses, including additional results in its appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains these original results and adds quantitative summarization evaluation on 300 validation examples, computational-cost estimates, and further qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The attention-gradient construction, S/E/W variants, hierarchical segmentation, and normalized-weight self-consistency objective are retained. v3 expands the explanation of initialization from ULTraS and training details without establishing a changed underlying algorithm.

E1.justification: The four vision datasets and the TL;DR and UltraFeedback data remain unchanged. Within TL;DR summarization, v3 adds evaluation with deliberately deleted context tokens, introducing a limited new perturbed-input scenario.

E2.justification: v3 adds uniform random token selection as a comparator in the quantitative summarization experiment (Figures 7 and 17). The segmentation comparator sets remain unchanged, including methods whose bibliographic references disappear.

E3.justification: v3 introduces a quantitative language evaluation using 300 randomly sampled validation examples, deletion budgets of 5–35%, a normalized summary log-probability metric, and equal-size random controls (Appendix H.2). Appendix B also introduces layer-dependent FLOP comparisons at batch size 64. Existing experiments' newly disclosed optimizer settings do not establish changed training.

E4.justification: v3 adds token-removal sensitivity analysis to test attribution faithfulness, computational-cost analysis, ULTraS-versus-ULTraW heatmap comparisons, a second multi-animal example, and six additional summarization cases. The original depth, ITIoU, and clustering-threshold analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces explicitly labeled one-standard-deviation error bars and bands for the Comprehensiveness curves; v2 has no corresponding uncertainty reporting. Neither version supplies repeated-run counts or seeds for these comparisons.

E6.justification: v3 adds Comprehensiveness-versus-selection-budget results, layerwise FLOP estimates, and qualitative findings. Most existing vision scores match, but ULTraE with DINO ViT-B/16 changes from 46.7 VOC mIoU in v2 Table 7 to 50.0 in v3 Table 2, without an accompanying reported setting change.

T1.justification: v3 introduces a task-specific normalized Comprehensiveness definition and summary-support formulation (Equations 16–20). The existing explanation-map, loss, ITIoU, and Transformer equations remain equivalent despite regrouping and renumbering; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain direct latent-token interpretation, training-free state-of-the-art unsupervised segmentation, improvement through the lightweight W extension, and applicability to vision and language. Splitting and elaborating the contribution list does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v3 adds mechanism hypotheses about using all tokens, projecting before aggregation, and sharpening heatmaps through ULTraW. It introduces stronger causal-faithfulness interpretations of the NLP results alongside specific limitations concerning sufficiency, paraphrase stability, human rationales, and model dependence. Existing dataset-labeling and computational limitations are largely retained or reorganized.

D1.justification: v3 adds a code repository link and specifies Adam, learning rate 0.01, batch size 32, and 10 epochs for the previously reported 256 training samples. It also documents ULTraS initialization and batch-size-specific computational costs. These extend reproducibility information without establishing that existing experiments were rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds DeYoung et al. (2020) for Comprehensiveness and Zhou et al. (2022) for Transformer robustness, and expands its distinction from INVITE. References for STEGO+HP, MaskDistill, and TransFGU disappear even though their comparison rows remain.

P1.justification: The introduction is reorganized around research questions and an expanded framework overview, with substantial revisions to method explanations and the concluding discussion. v3 also restructures the appendices, integrates former supplementary experimental material into the main text, and adds a broader-impact section.

P2.justification: v3 replaces the two-column main-text format with a journal layout, relocates Cityscapes/Potsdam and full perturbation tables, and incorporates the former ULTraE table into benchmark tables. It expands Figure 4 and adds computational, heatmap, and summarization displays. The new Comprehensiveness plot is repeated in the appendix.

improvement.justification: v3 improves reproducibility disclosures and quantifies the computational burden acknowledged in v2. However, its principal new NLP validation has a sign inconsistency: Equations 16–17 divide a confidence drop by a negative log-probability, reversing the stated higher-is-better interpretation. The PDFs cannot establish whether the formula or plotted computation is wrong. These useful additions and the compromised support for stronger faithfulness claims leave the net quality change uncertain.
